title: Khusro Bagh, Prayagraj - A Hidden Mughal Garden of History and Architecture
content:
Khusro Bagh, Prayagraj - A Hidden Mughal Garden of History and Architecture

Khusro Bagh is one of the most significant historical monuments in Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad). Spread over a vast area near Allahabad Junction Railway Station, this Mughal garden complex is famous for its grand tombs, Persian-style gardens, and rich historical background. It is a peaceful heritage site that reflects the architectural brilliance of the Mughal era.

History of Khusro Bagh

Khusro Bagh is named after Prince Khusro Mirza, the eldest son of Mughal Emperor Jahangir. After rebelling against his father, Khusro Mirza was imprisoned, and later his tomb was built here. The complex also houses the tombs of Shah Begum (Khusro’s mother) and Nithar Begum (Khusro’s sister). These tombs date back to the early 17th century and showcase the royal Mughal legacy.

Architectural Significance

The tombs at Khusro Bagh are excellent examples of Mughal architecture, featuring:

  • Intricate stone carvings
  • Persian-style arches and domes
  • Decorative floral motifs
  • Red sandstone and plaster work

The layout follows the traditional Charbagh (four-part garden) design, symbolizing paradise as described in Islamic tradition.

Role in Indian History

Khusro Bagh played an important role during the Indian freedom movement. It is believed that Chandrashekhar Azad stayed here during the revolutionary period, making it a place of national as well as historical importance.

Peaceful Garden Atmosphere

Today, Khusro Bagh is maintained as a protected monument and public garden. Lush greenery, wide walking paths, and historical surroundings make it a favorite spot for heritage lovers, photographers, and morning walkers.

Visitor Information

  • Location: Near Allahabad Junction, Prayagraj
  • Timings: Sunrise to sunset
  • Entry fee: Free
  • Photography: Allowed
